justification: A pairs bold sans headings with a serif body, so the section headings are clearly stronger and the numbered headings are easy to scan. B uses light-weight headings that are weak against the body text. B also splits 'dash-board' across lines with a hyphen, which hurts readability, and it has justified-looking letter spacing. B's blue rules do separate the sections, but they add clutter and don't make up for the weak headings. The header bands are similar.

Design B is more consistent: the rules, text and table share one left and right margin (about 84 to 556), and the Arabic heading and body sit flush right with the table edge. In A the margins are ragged. The English body is indented relative to the 'Overview' heading, the top rule is shorter than the second rule, and the Arabic heading overhangs the table edge. A's Arabic text in the table is tiny. B's Arabic is larger and easier to read, and its table has even padding. A's bold sans heading is stronger in hierarchy, but its misalignment hurts the overall result.

B aligns the heading, intro text and table on one left edge, giving a clean column. A indents the intro text and table relative to the headings, which looks slightly off. B's numbered headings and running header and footer (B2) help navigation. A has a vivid blue banner and a rule above each section heading, but its footer is sparse (A2). B's table is wider and consistent across both pages.

B uses bold sans numbered headings that stand out clearly from the serif body text. This gives a clear hierarchy, and the sections are easy to scan. A's light serif headings are close in weight to the body text, and its rules above each section add clutter and make it feel repetitive. A's References heading is also small and inconsistent with the other headings, which weakens the hierarchy. B's spacing is more even, and its header band is similar to A's.

A pairs bold sans section headings with a serif body, so the Income Statement and Balance Sheet headings stand out clearly (A1, A2). B uses light-weight headings in the same face as the body, which makes the hierarchy flatter (B1, B2). The tables are near-identical in both. B's header band on page 2 and its 'Page 2 of 2' footer are a nice touch, but they repeat the title and section name and add clutter. A's royal-blue banner is bolder, while B's navy is more restrained. Overall A has the clearer hierarchy.

A keeps one consistent left edge: title, rules, headings, body and table all align to the same margins. B's margins are inconsistent. Its Overview heading sits at the far left while the body text is indented, and the rules have different widths, with the second extending past the right edge of the table. The Arabic heading in B also overhangs the table edge. B's bolder sans heading is a nice touch, but its misalignment looks sloppy. A's table is wider and clearer.

A has a bold blue title band, sans-serif headings and thin rules that separate sections clearly, so the hierarchy is strong and the page looks designed. Its body text is indented, which sits slightly oddly against the left-aligned headings, and the content runs off-centre to the left. B is clean and consistent with numbered serif headings, but it is plain and has no visual anchor. Its References heading is larger than A's, which is slightly odd for a back-matter section.

Design B keeps one margin and one right edge: the rules, Arabic heading, Arabic text and table all share the same left and right edges, so it looks tidy and balanced. Design A has misaligned edges. The Overview heading sits at the far left while the body is indented, the rules have different lengths, and the Arabic heading overshoots the right edge of the table. A's serif/sans mix with tiny Arabic table text is also less coherent. B's Arabic is better sized and matches the Latin text. A's heading is bolder, but that does not offset its misalignment.

B's serif type, larger body text and roomier table rows read slightly better, and its spacing between sections is more even. A is crisper and more modern, but its text is smaller and the Arabic heading sits tight to the body line. Both leave the lower half of the page empty, so the difference is small.

A uses a clean sans-serif with a bold white title on a navy band. Its table header is crisp and heavier, and page 2 has a running header band ('Annual Financial Statements / Balance Sheet') plus a 'Page 2 of 2' footer. B's serif is elegant but lighter and smaller for dense numerals, its page 2 band is only a thin rule, and its footer is faint. The table splits differ: A breaks at 2024, B at 2023, and both repeat the header row. Layouts are otherwise similar, so the margin is modest.

Both are nearly identical RTL layouts with a header band, rules and short sections. B has slightly larger, bolder body text and clearer bullet glyphs (•, –). Its spacing between sections is also a little more generous, and the dark band is more neutral. A's smaller, lighter text and zero-like bullets read as weaker. A's blue band is a bit richer, but the difference is small.

A has a dark title band with white serif title and thin rules separating the sections, which gives a clear structure and a regular rhythm (A1). B is plain: a centered title and bold numbered headings in default Times, clean but generic (B1). A's headings are light and slightly small relative to their rules, and the References heading is weak. A's overall look is still more polished and deliberate.

Both pages share the same layout: a header band, ruled sections and a large empty lower half. A uses a more conventional Arabic typeface with lighter, even strokes and Arabic-Indic numerals that match the text, so it reads better. B's geometric font looks less natural for Arabic, and its numerals and percent sign look slightly awkward. B's dark navy band is sharp, while A's green band is also solid, so the bands are roughly equal.

Design B has consistent margins and a header band aligned with the content. Its Arabic text is larger and more legible, and the table fits the same column width as the body text. Design A has misaligned margins: the rule and heading start at the left edge while the body is indented, and the Arabic heading overhangs the right edge. A's Arabic table text and body text are tiny, so the two languages feel unbalanced. A's Arabic heading also stretches past the table edge.

B's navy title band, sans-serif headings and serif body give a clear hierarchy and a polished look (B1). A is plain, with a centered serif title and headings that blend into the body (A1). B numbers Abstract and References as sections, which is slightly odd but consistent. B's formula and footnote render a bit cleaner too.

A sets bold sans headings against a serif body, so the section headings stand out clearly (A1). B uses light serif headings that are close in weight to the body text, which weakens the hierarchy (B1). B's title band is dark and sober, but A's is the stronger accent. B's body text is small and thin. A's body is indented consistently and easier to read, though its headings sit left of the body, which is a slight misalignment.

A uses bold sans headings with a serif body, so the section titles stand out clearly (A1, A2). B's light-weight headings are weaker and the thin text is less legible (B1, B2). B's running header band on page 2 is a solid navy bar that looks heavier than A's subtle header rule. The tables are nearly identical in both designs. B's spacing is slightly more generous, but A's hierarchy and readability are stronger overall.

A uses a serif with a bold title and generous, even spacing between list items and sections. B uses a sans-serif with tighter list spacing, and the awkward hyphenated break 'dash-board' in the summary hurts readability. B's heading sizes are close to its body size, so its hierarchy is a little flatter. Both have a similar dark header band and rules.

A has bold numbered sans headings that read clearly against the serif body, and the Arabic heading carries its number. B's light serif headings are weaker, with no numbering, and the heading rules add clutter. Both tables are similar, and both leave the lower half of the page empty.

A pairs bold sans headings with a serif body, so section titles stand out clearly from the text (A1). B's headings are light-weight and close in weight to the body, which flattens the hierarchy (B1). B also hyphenates 'dash-board' and justifies the summary awkwardly. A's content is indented from its headings and its right margin is wider than the left, which unbalances the page. B's alignment is more consistent, with the title, headings and body sharing one left edge. A's spacing between sections is more even and A's headings are stronger overall.

A's serif face is refined, and its Arabic heading and body are larger, so the two languages carry similar weight (A1). B's headings are plainer, and its Arabic text is smaller than the Latin text, which weakens the bilingual match (B1). The tables and header bands are close to equal. B's bold table headers and its green band are a fair alternative, but A's overall polish is slightly stronger.

A has clearer Arabic letterforms, and its bullets and numerals render properly. B's bullets look like small zeros ('٠') and its numerals look like Latin '1' and '2', which makes the lists look glitchy. A's spacing between sections is more generous and even, with a larger gap after each rule. B is tighter, and its thin type is lighter and harder to read. Both have a solid header band and the same empty lower half.

Both pages share the same structure: a dark title band, ruled section headings and a centred formula. B uses a serif face with taller spacing, so the sections spread down the page with an even rhythm and a bold References heading that separates it from the body (B1). A is a clean sans, but its section blocks are tighter and leave a large empty area at the bottom (A1). A's body text is slightly easier to read in its sans face. B's serif body is small and light, though its generous leading helps. A's light-weight References heading barely stands out. The two are close overall, and B edges ahead.

Both pages share the same navy header band and short content, and leave the lower half empty. A adds blue rules above each section, which structure the page and give a steady rhythm. B numbers its headings, which helps hierarchy a little, but its bullets and numerals render more cleanly. A's bullet marks look like Arabic-Indic zeros ('٠') and its list numerals are small and weak, which hurts readability. Overall A's rules and fuller structure edge ahead, but A's odd bullet glyphs are a clear flaw. This is close.

A uses bold sans numbered headings that clearly separate sections from the serif body text. B has light serif headings with rules above each, which is elegant but weaker in contrast. B's 'References' heading is small and bold, unlike the other headings, so it is inconsistent. B's rules add some clutter and a heavy rhythm. Both title bands are similar.

B has bold headings that separate clearly from the serif body, so the hierarchy is stronger. The indented body creates a clear outline. B's content block sits slightly off-center with a larger right margin, and the justified text shows some loose spacing. A is clean and consistent, but its light headings are weaker, and its justified first paragraph breaks 'dash-board' awkwardly. B's heading and body pairing makes it slightly better.

A pairs a serif Latin face with a bolder Arabic face. This gives a more refined, editorial look and clearer title and heading contrast. B is clean but its light sans text is thin, and its Arabic is lighter. The table headers are bolder in B, but A's overall spacing between sections is slightly more generous and consistent. Both leave most of the page empty.

A uses a clean sans-serif Arabic face with numbered headings. Its "18%" figure is intact and the text is easy to read. B uses a thin serif face and its "18" is missing the percent sign. B's heading rules and the larger gaps between sections add structure, but the small, light body text is harder to read. B's saturated blue header band is slightly harsher than A's navy.

B uses a clean sans-serif Arabic face that stays legible, with larger body text. Its percent sign is present and its bullets are clear. A's body text is small and thin with a serif face, and the percent sign is missing from '18'. B's headings are also larger and easier to scan, and its band and rules are well proportioned. Both share the same layout.

B's bold sans headings with section numbers (B1) stand out more clearly than A's light serif headings (A1). B also keeps tighter spacing between sections, and its numbered headings help the reader tell the two language sections apart. A's rules above the headings are a nice touch, but its headings are weak next to the body text. The tables are nearly identical, and both pages leave the lower half empty.

A keeps title, rules, headings and body on one left margin, so the page is balanced and tidy. The serif headings and dark navy band look refined. B's headings sit at a far-left margin while the body is indented, and the right margin is wide and uneven, so the page looks lopsided. B's bold sans headings are stronger, but the layout is less cohesive.

B has a navy title band and thin blue rules between sections. These give clear structure and a regular rhythm. A is a plain serif page with bold headings. It is readable but generic. B's light-weight section headings are a little weak, and the References heading is smaller than the others. Even so, B looks more finished overall.

B puts a thin blue rule above each section, which separates the sections clearly and gives the page a steady rhythm. Its margins are wider, and the text block sits closer to the right edge of the page. A numbers the headings in Arabic-Indic numerals and has tighter spacing, so the sections feel less separated. In B the bullet glyph looks like a zero, a small flaw. Overall B is slightly more structured.

B uses a larger sans-serif Arabic face that is clearer and more legible, with a bigger title in a darker navy band. Its body text and rules align to a consistent right margin, and the percent sign is rendered properly. In A the body text is small and thin, the serif is light, the "18" has no percent sign, and the right edge is ragged: body text sits indented from the heading edge while the rules run wider. Both leave the lower half of the page empty.

Both designs carry the same table split across two pages. A uses an elegant serif title and headings, but its headings are light and small, so section hierarchy is weaker. A also has a rule line above each heading and a header rule on page 2 that looks thin. B uses bold sans headings with numbering, which gives clearer hierarchy and easier scanning. B also has a running header and a 'Page 2 of 2' footer, and its table is easier to read with firmer rules. A's page 2 footer is small and sits oddly at the left margin. B's header and footer are consistent, but its page 1 and 2 layouts are otherwise nearly the same as A's.

A uses a cleaner sans-serif Arabic face with clear size contrast between headings and body, and its heading, rules, and body text all share one right edge. In B the serif text is smaller and thinner, the headings sit further right than the body, and the '18%' shows a missing percent sign and awkward spacing. B's blue band is fine, but its alignment is looser. Both pages leave a large empty area at the bottom.

A pairs a refined serif title on a dark navy band with a consistent serif body. Its header and heading sit on the same left margin as the table, so the page feels aligned. B's bold sans headings sit left of the indented body text and table, which looks misaligned, and its bright blue band is heavier. A's page 2 also has a thin top rule, and its footer is tidy. Both tables are similar, with repeated headers and zebra-like row lines.

A keeps the title, headings and body on one left margin, so the page is cleanly aligned and balanced. Its body text is ragged-right and easy to read. B has headings hanging out to the left with the body indented, and the title sits on a different indent from the headings. B's rules end well short of the right edge, leaving an unbalanced right margin. B's justified paragraph shows loose word spacing. B's rules do separate the sections clearly, but the layout feels less coherent.

A pairs bold sans headings with a serif body, and its numbered headings (1 Overview, 2 نظرة عامة) are clearly stronger than the light-weight headings in B. B adds rules above each section, which helps structure, but its thin headings are weak and its single-family text looks flatter. Both tables and header bands are similar, and both leave the lower half of the page empty.

B's bold numbered headings stand out clearly from the serif body text, so the sections are easy to scan. In A the headings are light-weight and close in size to the body, and the many blue rules add clutter and flatten the hierarchy. B's spacing is also more even and open. A's tiny sans body text is slightly harder to read. The title bands are about equal.

A separates sections with thin rules and generous spacing, so the structure is clear and the rhythm is even. B numbers its headings, which adds a little hierarchy, but the numbers clash with the numbered list in the recommendations. B's tighter spacing also makes it feel more cramped. Both have a header band and large empty space at the bottom.

B is more cohesive: a serif-only scheme with a dark navy band, left-aligned text and a margin balanced on both sides. A has a heavy sans heading paired with a justified serif body, which opens up uneven word gaps in the summary. A's content also sits off-center, with a wider right margin, and its bright blue band is louder. A's bold headings do give slightly stronger hierarchy, but B's lighter headings are still clear and its vertical spacing is more even.

B uses a clean sans-serif with larger, clearer headings and body text, and it keeps the percent sign in the summary text. A's serif Arabic is small and light, and the summary line is mis-set with a gap before the number and no percent sign. B's rules, text and header band are better proportioned, and its dark navy band is more restrained. Both leave the lower half of the page empty.

Both share the same layout, so the differences are small. B has a bold sans title on a stronger navy band and a running header band on page 2 (B2). Its table rows are slightly more evenly spaced and its sans-serif figures are clearer. A's serif is elegant, but its light-weight figures are smaller and its page 2 has only a thin top rule (A2). B also adds a clear 'Page 2 of 2' footer.

A keeps one consistent left margin and a clean RTL mirror: the Arabic heading and body are right-aligned to the same margins, and the section numbers stay with the headings. The Arabic text is a comparable size and the table aligns with the text. B has ragged, inconsistent indents: the 'Overview' heading sits outside the body indent, the Arabic heading overshoots the right margin, and the rules run to different lengths. B's Arabic text and table cells are also small.

A has a strong navy title band, but its section headings are light-weight and barely larger than the body text, so the section hierarchy is weak. The many rules make the page feel segmented, and the small light text is harder to read (A1). B uses bold serif headings, numbered sections and a centered title, which give clear hierarchy and comfortable reading with generous spacing (B1). B is the cleaner, more readable academic layout, though A's title band is more striking.

B has bold numbered headings (1 Overview, 2 نظرة عامة) that set a clear hierarchy, with a serif body that pairs well with the sans headings. A's headings are light and only slightly larger than the body, so they barely register as headings. A's thin rules above each section add structure, but its light text is weaker. Both leave most of the page empty. The tables are similar, and B's header rule is a little crisper.

A keeps one consistent left and right margin, so rules, headings, body and table align, and the Arabic block mirrors the English one. The Arabic text and table are a readable size. B has misaligned margins: the Overview heading sits further left than its indented body, the rules end at different right edges, and the Arabic heading overshoots the right edge. B's Arabic text in the table is tiny, and the sans heading clashes with the serif body. B's blue band is bold but less refined than A's dark band.

B pairs a serif Latin face with a bolder Arabic face, which looks more refined. Its Arabic heading and body are larger and more legible, and its table has more generous row spacing and clearer rules (B1). A's thin sans Latin and light Arabic text feel weak next to the heavy title, and its table is tighter (A1). Both leave the bottom half of the page empty.

B pairs bold sans section headings with a serif body. Its numbered headings (B1, B2) are heavier and clearer than A's light-weight headings. B's table has slightly taller rows, and its header rule and bottom rule are cleaner on B2. A's running header band on page 2 is a solid dark bar, which is a stronger anchor, and A's thin rules above its headings are a nice touch. But A's light headings are weak in hierarchy. Overall the two are close, and B is slightly more readable.

A uses a sturdier serif that reads better at body size, and its Arabic text is balanced against the Latin. B's body text is lighter and smaller, so it looks faint, and its Arabic looks heavier than the Latin. The layouts and tables are otherwise nearly the same. A's green band is warm, while B's navy band is also fine.

A uses thin rules to separate sections, with indented body text that gives the page a clear structure and rhythm (A1). Its title band is a vivid blue and the Montserrat headings are strong. The drawbacks are that the right margin is wider than the left, so the content sits off-center, and the justified summary text has uneven word spacing. B is cleaner and more evenly balanced, with consistent margins and numbered headings, but it has no dividers, so it feels plainer and the sections blend together a little more (B1).

A uses bold sans headings with section numbers, so the headings stand out clearly from the serif body. B's headings are light and small, and its rules between sections add some rhythm but weaken the hierarchy. The tables are nearly identical. Both leave the lower half of the page empty. A's header band is navy and strong, and B's is darker and plainer.

A uses bold numbered sans headings against a serif body, so sections are easy to tell apart (A1). B's headings are light-weight and barely larger than the body text, and the 'References' heading is smaller than the others. The blue rules in B add structure but not enough emphasis to make up for the weak headings (B1). Both have the same header band and formula placement.

Both share the same layout: a header band, an English section, an Arabic section and a bilingual table, with the lower half of the page empty. A uses a serif that pairs well with the Arabic text and has slightly larger body text, so it reads a little more easily (A1). B's sans-serif is cleaner but its body text is smaller and lighter, and its Arabic looks thinner (B1). The tables are nearly identical.

A has a navy title band with a white bold title and sans headings paired with a serif body. This gives a clear hierarchy and a more polished look (A1). B is plain Times with a centered title and unnumbered Abstract and References. It reads as a default document and is less distinctive (B1). Spacing is similar in both.

Design A uses a clean sans-serif Arabic typeface with clear heading and body sizes. Its rules and text share a right edge and the margins are consistent (A1). In Design B the serif Arabic body is smaller and thinner, the summary line sits indented from the heading's right edge, and the heading and bullets are misaligned. Its rules also run wider than the text (B1). B's brighter blue band is fine but not better than A's.

A keeps one left edge: the title, headings, rules and body all align, with margins that look symmetric. The serif type is elegant and the dark navy band is restrained. B hangs its headings at the left of the rules while the body is indented, and the rules stop short of the right margin, so the page looks lopsided. B's justified paragraph leaves loose word spacing. B's bold sans headings are strong, but the saturated blue band and the mixed alignment make it less cohesive.

B uses a clean sans-serif Arabic face with larger, clearer headings and body text, and its numbered sections align to one right edge. A's small serif text looks cramped. Its thin rules separate sections but leave the body text indented away from the headings. A's text is small, and its '18' lacks a percent sign, which B includes. A's brighter blue band is heavier, while B's navy band is calmer. Both pages leave the lower half empty.

A pairs a serif body with a bold white title on a dark band, which reads as a more academic and polished document. Its References heading is bold, so it is distinct from the section headings. A's spacing between sections is more generous and even. B is clean, but its sans-serif text is smaller and lighter. B's References heading is plain and looks weak, and its sections are more cramped.

A uses bold sans-serif numbered headings ("1 Income Statement", "2 Balance Sheet") that stand out clearly against the serif body, and a running header on page 2 aids navigation. B's light, regular-weight headings are weak and barely distinguishable from the body text. The tables are nearly identical in both. B's top rules and footer are tidy, but its hierarchy is flatter. A's header band is slightly brighter and stronger.

B has a dark title band with white title and thin rules separating sections. This gives clear structure and a consistent rhythm (B1). A is plain: bold headings are legible and numbered, but the page looks generic with a centered title and no separators (A1). B's References heading is small and inconsistent with the other headings, and its light section headings are weaker than A's bold ones. Even so, B's banding and dividers make it the more polished document overall.

A aligns headings, intro text and table on one left margin, and numbered section headings plus a running header and 'Page 2 of 2' footer give clear structure (A1, A2). B indents the body and table relative to the headings, which looks misaligned, and adds rules above headings that add clutter (B1, B2). B's brighter blue band is more saturated and less refined than A's navy band, though its centered title is balanced. Both repeat the table header on page 2 and leave the same empty space at the bottom of page 2.

B uses bold sans headings with section numbers, so the heading levels stand out clearly from the serif body text (B1). A uses light serif headings at nearly body weight, which makes them look weak. Its rules between sections add structure and an even rhythm, but they do not make up for the weak headings (A1). A's text is slightly smaller and lighter, so B is easier to read. Both title bands are similar.

B adds thin rules above each section, which separate the sections clearly and give a steadier rhythm. Its larger text and spacing are easy to read. A has numbered headings and a slightly more refined typeface, but its sections run together with less separation. Both leave the lower half of the page empty, and both use a dark header band.

B adds thin rules above each section and spaces the sections more evenly. This separates them clearly and gives a steadier vertical rhythm. B's headings are slightly larger and have no numerals. A's numbered headings sit tight to the body text, and the whole layout feels more cramped. Both use a solid header band and leave the lower half of the page empty. B's content block is better placed and a little fuller.

A uses a clean geometric Arabic sans with clear size contrast between headings and body. The text is legible and the dark navy band is sober. B uses a small, thin serif-style Arabic face that looks weak. Its headings are only slightly larger than the body, and the percent sign is missing from the number. A's rules are aligned to the text block and its spacing is more even, so A reads better.

Design B has bolder, more legible headings, with a sans heading face that stands out against the serif body text (B1). Design A uses light serif headings with thin rules, which look elegant but weaker in hierarchy; the Arabic text is also small (A1). Both leave the lower page empty and have similar tables. B's numbered headings and tighter grouping give a clearer structure, though the '2' placement in the Arabic heading is slightly odd.

Both pages share the same layout: a header band, rules and right-aligned Arabic sections. B uses a more conventional Arabic typeface with clearer Arabic-Indic numerals (١٨٪, ١ and ٢). Its body text is a little larger and its right margin is tighter, so the text sits more naturally against the rules. A's rounder geometric font looks slightly lighter, and its numerals are less clear. The dark green band in B looks richer than A's navy, but both are fine. The lower half of each page is empty, so they are equal on that point.

B gives the Arabic text a size and weight that match the English, and its Arabic table cells are legible. B's margins and left edges are consistent, and its two language blocks mirror each other. In A the Arabic body and table text is tiny next to the English, and the Arabic heading overhangs the right margin. A's indents and rules are also misaligned: the Overview heading sits at the margin while the body is indented. A has a stronger blue band and heading hierarchy, but its Arabic is hard to read and its alignment is inconsistent (A1, B1).

A has more generous spacing between sections and a clearer bullet glyph and heading size. The dark navy band is sober, and its margins are consistent. B is more compact, with its bullets rendered as small zeros that look odd. B's body text is slightly smaller. The two are otherwise very similar.

A keeps the title, headings and body on one left margin. Its numbered headings are bold and evenly spaced, so the page reads cleanly and consistently. B indents the body relative to the headings and leaves the right margin wide and unbalanced. Its rules add clutter, and its small References heading is inconsistent with the other headings. B's blue band is vivid, but its title is indented differently from the headings below it.

B has a strong blue title band, sans-serif headings paired with a serif body, and thin rules that divide the sections clearly (B1). A is plain, with a centred title and uniform serif headings, so it looks like a default document (A1). B's indented body text and rules give a clearer scan path. B's lopsided right margin and the smaller References heading are minor drawbacks.

B has larger, clearer Arabic text, proper bullets and Arabic-Indic numerals, and more generous spacing between sections. A's text is smaller and lighter, and its bullets render as odd small digits (٠) instead of bullets, which looks like a glyph error. Both have a header band and rules, and both leave the lower half of the page empty.

Design A hyphenates 'dash-board' across a line break in the summary, which hurts readability, and its text is tight and small. Design B uses a serif face with more generous line spacing, fills the page more evenly, and keeps the link intact on one line. Both share the same dark header band and rule structure, so they differ little there. B's vertical rhythm between sections is more even, and its list spacing is airier.

A keeps one sans family and aligns the headings, intro text and table to the same left edge. Its running header band on page 2 and the 'Page 2 of 2' footer make it feel more finished (A2). B indents the body text and table relative to the headings, which looks misaligned (B1, B2). B's serif table text mixed with sans headings is less cohesive, and its brighter blue band is heavier. The two designs are otherwise very close.

A separates its sections with thin rules and gives them generous spacing, so the rhythm is clearer and the sections read as distinct blocks (A1). B numbers its headings and is more compact, but it has no dividers. B's headings stay close to their body text, so the sections blend together more (B1). Both use a similar header band and leave the bottom half of the page empty.

B uses bold sans headings with a serif body, so sections are easy to tell apart (B1). A's light-weight headings are close in weight to the body text, which flattens the hierarchy and weakens scanning (A1). B's indented body under flush-left headings adds structure, but the content block sits left-heavy with a wider right margin. A's banner is a calmer navy and its margins are even. B's brighter blue banner is stronger, though its title is indented differently from the headings.

A pairs a bold blue title band, with a white sans-serif title, with bold sans section headings. That gives a clear hierarchy (A1). B's dark band and light serif 'Income Statement' heading are weaker and less distinct from the body text (B1). B also has a stray rule across the top of page 2. Both tables are clean with repeated headers, though B's table is slightly larger and splits at 2023/2024 rather than 2024/2025. Both leave the second page mostly empty. A's bolder headings and band make it easier to scan.

Design B has bold numbered headings that stand out clearly, and its serif body text pairs well with them. It also avoids the awkward hyphenated break 'dash-board' that A has in the summary.
